content.topic: Treatment of right ventricular failure in acute high-risk pulmonary embolism
content.notes: Page contains treatment strategies (volume optimization, vasopressors/inotropes, mechanical circulatory support) and abbreviations (CO, BP, ECMO, RV). 'Epinephrine is used in cardiac arrest.'

table_rows.properties_and_use: Increases RV inotropy, lowers filling pressures
table_rows.caveats: May aggravate arterial hypotension if used alone without a vasopressor; may trigger or aggravate arrhythmias

table_rows.properties_and_use: Rapid short-term support combined with oxygenator
table_rows.caveats: Complications with use over longer periods (>5–10 days), including bleeding and infections; no clinical benefit unless combined with surgical embolectomy; requires an experienced team

table_rows.properties_and_use: Saline or Ringer's lactate, ~500 mL over 15–30 min; consider in patients with normal/low central venous pressure (eg, concomitant hypovolaemia)
table_rows.caveats: Volume loading can over-distend the RV, worsen ventricular interdependence, and reduce CO

table_rows.properties_and_use: Increases RV inotropy and systemic BP, promotes positive ventricular interactions, and restores coronary perfusion gradient
table_rows.caveats: Excessive vasoconstriction may worsen tissue perfusion

other.epinephrine_note: Epinephrine is used in cardiac arrest (footnote).
